transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-10-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Narayanan (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (CTO - Saffron), Lina Park (Cloud Architect), Daniel Wu (Security Engineer)

Summary: Short discovery to validate Saffron's network and compliance constraints for a Private/VPC deployment. Focus on peering topology, egress, region restrictions, and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. quick roll call?
[00:04] Marcus (Saffron): Marcus here.
[00:06] Lina (Saffron): Lina on the call.
[00:08] Daniel (Saffron): Daniel also here.
[00:10] Jordan: great. priya from our infra team is with me - priya, do you want to intro?
[00:15] Priya (Redwood): hi all, priya narayanan, infra/solutions at Redwood. i'll focus on the network and deployment constraints.
[00:21] Jordan: high level agenda — understand your stack, region/residency needs, CIDR and egress requirements, and agree next steps.

[02:10] Marcus: quick context — we're building a document-cognition product, heavy PII in EU. must keep EU workload in EU region. APAC is optional but we'd rather keep latency under 60ms for APAC users. also, security team needs static egress IP for allowlisting with partner APIs.
[02:36] Priya: understood. do you currently run multi-region in house or cloud?
[02:40] Lina: we're primarily on AWS with us-east-1 and eu-west-1. for APAC we have a presence in ap-southeast-1 but it's lower capacity. our VPC CIDRs are 10.10.0.0/16 (us), 10.20.0.0/16 (eu), 10.30.0.0/16 (apac).

[05:02] Priya: ok good — three non-overlapping blocks, that's easier. are you using a transit gateway today?
[05:08] Lina: yes, transit gw in us-east and eu-west, peer via TGW attachments. some sites use DirectConnect to onprem.
[05:20] Daniel: also we have a central firewall that requires egress NAT for third parties, so outbound flows must come from a known / stable IP.

[07:40] Jordan: that matches common asks. couple options from Redwood: Private deployment (customer VPC peered to Redwood private endpoints) or Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs in your VPC via peering / private endpoints). both can give you control over network egress. Priya: can you walk topology options?
[07:58] Priya: sure. Option A: VPC Peering to Redwood private endpoints in the same region — simple, but peering is regional and won't route across regions so you'd need separate peering per region. Option B: AWS PrivateLink/Private Endpoint to a managed endpoint — supports cross-account private connectivity and scales well for security teams. Option C: we can also place a Dedicated cluster in your VPC (Redwood Dedicated) so traffic never leaves your network fabric; that helps with latency and residency.

[10:12] Marcus: on PrivateLink — does that require us to open specific ports? we have strict firewall rules.
[10:18] Priya: PrivateLink uses ENIs and you talk over TCP over the private interface, you don't need inbound firewall ports to the Redwood infra — you allow outbound to the PrivateLink endpoint's IPs. we also provide a list of prefix ranges for allowlisting. note though PrivateLink availability varies by region and provider — we support AWS PrivateLink in most commercial regions but APAC has some gaps.

[12:01] Lina: APAC availability is our concern. if Redwood doesn't have PrivateLink in ap-southeast-1, we'd need either to route traffic via eu-west or run a local dedicated cluster in apac which is costlier. what's the recommended approach?
[12:22] Priya: two approaches — run a small Dedicated nodepool in ap-southeast-1 for APAC latency, or route APAC users to eu-west with an edge proxy, but that increases latency. for guarded data, we recommend regional deployment to avoid cross-border transfer controls.

[14:40] Daniel: about static egress — can Redwood guarantee a fixed IP block per deployment? we need this for partner allowlist.
[14:47] Jordan: yes, Redwood can allocate static egress ranges when deployed in your VPC or via NAT through a customer-managed egress. if you host a Dedicated cluster in your VPC the egress uses your NAT/IGW so IPs are yours. for PrivateLink we can also publish stable endpoint IPs but internals may change if you use multi-az; we'll provide a canonical list.

[17:05] Priya: another note — customers often front Redwood endpoints with their own proxy/NAT to centralize egress. that gives you a single known egress IP and lets you route model calls through your firewall and DLP.

[18:30] Marcus: what about overlapping CIDR? we already saw some vendors ask us to renumber. we can't renumber easily.
[18:38] Priya: we avoid overlap by requiring unique peering blocks. if your VPCs are overlapping we can do PrivateLink which uses endpoint ENIs in your VPC and doesn't require non-overlapping ranges the same way peering does. but peering requires distinct CIDRs. so PrivateLink is often the workaround for overlap.

[20:55] Lina: are there implications for route tables and BGP with our transit gateway? we want to centralize routing.
[21:02] Priya: if you use TGW, we can attach the Redwood VPC to the TGW and advertise routes; alternatively, you can create a peering per region and propagate routes via TGW. we'll need route table screenshots and the TGW attachments to plan.

[23:40] Daniel: security controls — SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration. we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys and if audit logs can be shipped to our SIEM.
[23:50] Jordan: yes. KMS/HSM integration is supported in Private deployments; customers can provide key envelopes via KMS and we integrate for at-rest. audit logs are available and we can stream to your S3 or cloud logging. we'll include the technical integration doc in the security pack.

[26:10] Marcus: compliance question — our legal team wants model inference and logs to stay in EU for EU work. can Redwood pin model weights and inference to the eu-west region?
[26:20] Priya: yes — we can pin deployments and model placement. for Dedicated we can pin the nodepool to eu-west-1. For Private endpoints you choose where the service runs and we can prevent cross-region routing for that tenant. we do need to confirm support for every specific model variant in a region — sometimes the latest quantized model has limited region availability, we'll flag compatibility.

[28:35] Lina: what about fallback? if eu capacity is exhausted do requests fail over to US? we need to avoid unexpected cross-border fails.
[28:44] Jordan: we have smart routing policies and graceful degradation. by default we won't fail open across regions for Private deployments unless configured. we can set hard rules: no-failover cross-region. for Hosted customers we have fallback options but for your use-case we'd lock to region for EU workloads.

[31:05] Marcus: network perf benchmarks — can we run a quick latency test from our APAC VPC to a Redwood endpoint?
[31:12] Priya: yes — we can spin up a test PrivateLink endpoint or a temporary dedicated test instance in the region. we'll plan that in the network workshop.

[33:20] Daniel: procurement question — how long to get Dedicated up? we have timeline: pilot by end of Q4, production in Q1.
[33:30] Jordan: typical Dedicated pilot is 2-4 weeks for provisioning and config once contracts signed and network is ready. if we do PrivateLink it can be quicker — a few days after VPC exchange and peering setup.

[35:10] Lina: do you have a preferred IP range size for endpoint ENIs? we want to avoid wasting space in our CIDR.
[35:16] Priya: endpoints usually need a /28 per AZ for ENIs; Dedicated nodepools depend on cluster size. we'll send a sizing doc and recommended CIDR carve-outs.

[37:55] Jordan: circling back — main blockers we heard: APAC region availability for PrivateLink, static egress IPs, and confirmation of KMS and audit log export. agreed?
[38:03] Marcus: yes. also timeline sensitivity — pilot end of Q4.

[39:20] Priya: we'll follow up with three artifacts: 1) Private deployment checklist with CIDR templates and endpoint IP ranges, 2) SOC2/ISO + KMS integration doc, 3) Dedicated pilot sizing and pricing PDF.

[40:40] Daniel: one small thing — our partners require mutual TLS to partner APIs. can Redwood originate mTLS from your side if we let traffic go via Redwood egress?
[40:49] Priya: Redwood can support mTLS origination when using Dedicated in-customer VPC or via approved egress proxy patterns. we'll confirm exact pattern in the workshop.

[42:55] Marcus: let's set the workshop. Lina and Daniel will prepare VPC screenshots and firewall rules.
[43:04] Jordan: i'll schedule a 90-minute slot and include Priya and our networking PM. suggested slots: Oct 24 or 25.

[44:30] Jordan: any competitive sensitivities to flag? Marcus?
[44:35] Marcus: main comparison is to an internal infra build and Anthropic. decision will be on speed to market vs build cost.

[45:10] Priya: last note — we'll include a fallback plan that avoids cross-border inference for EU traffic by configuration.

[46:00] Jordan: thanks everyone. quick recap of next steps: jordan sends security and pricing pack; priya drafts CIDR/peering plan; lina shares network screenshots; schedule workshop.
[46:20] Marcus: thanks all.
[46:25] Lina: thanks.
[46:26] Daniel: bye.

[48:00] Meeting ends.
